L000100	 Existence of  lower bounds for energy-type expressions  has fundamental importance for well-posedness of every theory, and is closely related to the global behaviour of solutions of the equations.
L000101	
L000102	In the context of the AdS/CFT correspondence, a natural notion of energy is the holographic one~\cite{Papadimitriou:2005ii}, see also \cite{Henningson:1998gx,deHaro:2000vlm,Balasubramanian:1999re,Skenderis:2000in,Cheng:2005wk},
L000103	which {can be} defined for spacetimes that locally approach Anti-de Sitter at infinity. Such spacetimes have a timelike conformal boundary, $\scri$.
L000104	Given a vector field $X$ on $\scri$,   a section $S$
L000105	of $\scri$, and a metric $g$
L000106	as made precise below,
L000107	we write   $ {Q[S,X]}(g)$ for the holographic charge of $g$ defined as
L000108	
L000109	\begin{equation}\label{25I26.2}
L000110	   {Q[S,X]}(g) =
L000111	  -
L000112	   \int_S t^A{}_B X^B ds_A
L000113	  \,,
L000114	\end{equation}
L000115	
L000116	where $t^A{}_B$ is the
L000117	holographic energy-momentum tensor of $g$.
L000118	The holographic energy is obtained by choosing $X=\partial_t$. This energy is reasonably well understood when the    metric at  $\scri$ is
L000119	 conformal to an ultrastatic metric with Einstein space-sections,
L000120	 in which case the
L000121	 holographic energy essentially coincides \cite[Equation~(17)]{Skenderis:2000in}
L000122	 with the more usual hyperbolic energy~\cite{ChAIHP,AshtekarDas,HT,AbbottDeser}. For these last metrics several positivity and rigidity theorems are available~\cite{ChHerzlich,Wang,ChGPotaux,ChDelayHPETv1,
L000123	ChGallowayHPET,
L000124	Rallabhandi:2025kti,YiYueHirsch,HuangJangMartin,Hirsch:2025usn,
L000125	BrendleHung,BrendleHung2,GibbonsGPI,GHHP,LeeNeves,GallowayTsang},
L000126	but nothing has been known so far beyond these cases.
L000127	\checking{no logs here whatever the dimension, see Section~\ref{s21III26.1a}}

L000129	The aim of this letter is to point out that
L000130	{\redc a suitably weighted
L000131	  holographic energy (see \eqref{25I26.3} below)
L000132	  }
L000133	  is positive
L000134	for all four-dimensional solutions $(\mcM,g)$ of the Einstein equations with a negative cosmological constant,
L000135	with a conformally static conformal infinity
L000136	
L000137	\footnote{
L000138	A construction of large classes of static vacuum solutions can be found in~\cite{ACD2}. A class of negative-mass solutions (which do not satisfy the hypotheses of our positivity theorem here) can be found in~\cite{ChDelayGluing,CDW}.
L000139	},

L000157

L000839	Every Lorentzian metric $g$ with the  conformal structure on $\scri $ given by \eqref{7II25.1}, which satisfies the dominant energy condition and which is vacuum to sufficiently high order, on a manifold which has a partial Cauchy surface $\hyp$  inducing the trivial spin structure on $\hyp\cap\scri$,  has positive charge $Q[\hyp\cap\scri,\partial_u](g)$. A similar statement holds for  higher-dimensional Siklos waves.
L000840	
L000841	
L000842	
L000843	Let $\zg$ be static and let $g$ and $\zg$ share the same conformal structure on $\scri$. When both metrics are, say, vacuum it was shown in~\cite{ChWutteEnergy} that the functional
L000844	
L000845	\begin{align}\label{25I26.6}
L000846	  {Q[S,\partial_t]}(g) -  {Q[S,\partial_t]}(\zg)
L000847	\end{align}
L000848	
L000849	is a Noether charge
L000850	(compare~\cite{Papadimitriou:2005ii,HollandsIshibashiMarolf})
L000851	equal to the Hamiltonian energy of $g$ relative to $\zg$.
L000852	Recall that a perturbative analysis of the positivity of mass goes back to~\cite{AbbottDeser}, where a quadratic expansion of the energy around the Anti-de Sitter metrics confirmed positivity  for nearby metrics; compare~\cite{BCN}. Now, the calculations in that last reference have been carried out for perturbations of any static metrics, in any dimension. In particular the calculations
L000853	there are directly relevant to  static vacuum metrics near the Anti-de Sitter metric, constructed in~\cite{ChDelayKlinger,ACD2}, which are parameterised by conformally static conformal structures. These are
L000854	 stationary points of energy, thus have a Taylor expansion in terms of the perturbations of the metric which starts with quadratic terms. Since the second-derivative operator of the energy functional is strictly positive at the Anti-de Sitter metric, and depends continuously upon the metric,  the arguments in~\cite{BCN}, including the possibility of realising a suitable gauge, prove  positivity of Hamiltonian mass
L000855	
L000856	\footnote{We are grateful to Klaus Kröncke for pointing this out.}
L000857	
L000858	near these metrics, and hence of \eqref{25I26.6}, in all spacetime dimensions $n+1\ge 3$
L000859	\footnote{See~\cite{ChWutte, Chrusciel:2024vle} for $n=2$.}.
L000860	
L000861	In $3+1$-dimensions we hence obtain
L000862	two independent
L000863	 inequalities, namely \eqref{25I26.3} with $ {\widetilde X}=\partial_t$
L000864	 and
L000865	
L000866	\begin{align}\label{25I26.6wer}
L000867	 \red{Q[S,\partial_t]}(g) \ge  \red{Q[S,\partial_t]}(\zg)
L000868	\end{align}
L000869	
L000870	  when a
L000871	  vacuum metric $g$ is close to a vacuum
L000872	  static background $\zg$, both sharing the same induced geometry at $\scri$,  and when $\zg$ itself is close to  the AdS metric. Under these restrictions, equality in \eqref{25I26.6wer} occurs only
L000873	  when   $g=\zg$.
L000874	
L000875	Note that we have been concentrating on spacetime dimension four, because the requirement of convergence, as $\epsilon\to 0$, of the volume integral of \eqref{3V25.1} in spacetime dimension $n+1$ requires $|\nabla\psi|= O(x^{\frac{n-1}{2} +\epsilon})$ for some $\epsilon > 0$, which might impose more conditions on the boundary geometry when $n>3$. It is tempting to conjecture that positivity of $Q_{CW}$ holds in all spacetime dimensions $n+1\ge 4$ for all conformally static $\scri$'s with sections which carry solutions of the
L000876	 $(n-1)$-dimensional twistor  equation:
L000877	
L000878	\begin{equation}
L000879	\Big( \delta_{\hbone}^{ \hbtwo}
L000880	 + \frac{1}{(n-1)}  \gamma_{\hbone}  \gamma^{\hbtwo}
L000881	  \Big)
L000882	    \zmcD_{\ze_\hbtwo} \zpsi = 0 \,;
L000883	     \label{eqspinnnew}
L000884	\end{equation}
L000885	
L000886	cf.\ e.g.~\cite{BaumEtAl,ginoux2009dirac}.
L000887	The fact that the conjecture is true in $(3+1)$-dimensions has been shown above; it
L000888	 is true in $(4+1)$-dimensions by calculations identical to the above together with the last paragraph of \cite[Section 6]{Cheng:2005wk}.

L000900	\section{Conclusions}
L000901	In this letter  we established positivity of
L000902	{\redc the  weighted holographic energy \eqref{25I26.3}
L000903	}
L000904	for four-dimensional spacetimes
L000905	with or without black hole boundaries, with conformally
L000906	 static infinity,
L000907	 with spherical cross-sections of infinity, or with toroidal cross-sections with a compatible spin structure.
L000908	 We further established positivity of a holographic charge associated with a null conformal Killing vector for conformal boundary geometries induced by a Siklos wave in all dimensions.
L000909	  Our argument exploits
L000910	 existence of solutions to the twistor equation on sections of the conformal boundary.
L000911	The same method applies to prove positivity for all $(4+1)$-dimensional spacetimes  which possess a conformally static boundary geometry at infinity with sections which admit solutions of the three-dimensional twistor equation. We conjecture that a similar statement holds true in all spacetime dimension greater than five.
L000912	
L000913	{\redc
L000914	Since
L000915	
L000916	\begin{equation}\label{20III.1}
L000917	   \red{Q_{CW}[S,\bar X]}(g) \equiv  \red{Q [S,e^{-u}\bar X]}(g)
L000918	   \,,
L000919	\end{equation}
L000920	
L000921	one can instead think of $Q_{CW}$ as the usual holographic charge with respect to a rescaled vector field. Now,  the divergence theorem shows that $ Q [S,\partial_t](g) $ is independent of $S$  when $\partial_t$ is a conformal Killing vector of the boundary geometry because $t_{AB}$ is transverse and traceless in odd space dimensions.
L000922	But $\red{Q_{CW}[S,\partial_t]}(g) $ will depend upon $S$ in general because $e^{-u}\partial_t$ is not a conformal Killing vector
L000923	 on $\scri$ unless $u$ is constant.
L000924	This implies that  $ Q_{CW}  $    can be radiated away, which can be considered as a desirable feature, with positivity providing an upper bound on the amount of charge that can be emitted.
L000925	
L000926	Our result should be contrasted with the analysis in~\cite{HicklingWiseman}, where it is proved
L000927	 that $(3+1)$-dimensional \emph{static} vacuum conformally
L000928	   smooth metrics with conformally compact static slices
L000929	 without boundary have \emph{negative or zero holographic} energy; recall that many such metrics exist near Anti-de Sitter spacetime by~\cite{ACD, ACD2}.
L000930	 It is rather counterintuitive that the introduction of the conformal factor arising from the solutions of the twistor equation changes the sign of the charge integrals, as follows from our analysis. This implies in particular that the integrand of \eqref{25I26.2} can  have a constant sign for
L000931	 such
L000932	 metrics only if it vanishes.
L000933	}
